 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Michael Porter Jr. isn't one to shy away from speaking openly about himself and his family background. He has emerged as one of the league's most outspoken players today. While it is due in part to his controversial statements, it is also due to his ability to express his authenticity.
 One thing he isn't afraid to comment on is his complicated relationship with women. Speaking on the "Girls, Disrupted Podcast," MPJ explained that even during his strict upbringing, he would always get in trouble because of girls, and it led to him being phone-less for an entire year.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Strict parents 
 Porter was raised in Missouri under a strict Christian family. Not to mention that he grew up with seven siblings. Despite his large family, however, his parents never failed to enforce strict supervision, especially with him, who, at one point, was the best high school prospect in the country.
 "They like kept me locked up, like if I was texting girls and stuff, they were strict," he shared . "If I wanted to go to a high school football game, my mom was like, 'Okay, I'm going to go with you then." 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Another reason MPJ was tightly parented was that he was his parents' first boy after their two older sisters. He considered himself his parents' guinea pig for raising a boy before his younger brothers were born.
 Porter's parents were ultimately protecting him from making the wrong decision s that could derail his career back then, which, unfortunately for him, meant strict control over his social life and even his screen time.
 Running away 
 The restrictions became so strict that Porter even recalled his parents downloading software on his phone, which he only got when he was in seventh grade, that could monitor his texts. Some teenagers would be wary of using their phones if they knew their parents were watching. But like any other adolescent, MPJ wanted to socialize, especially with girls.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement MPJ recalled always texting girls on his phone, getting caught by his parents, and having it confiscated. It came to a point where Porter continued texting girls, and his parents decided it was enough and punished him.
 "I got my phone taken for a whole year. They kept catching me texting girls. They'd take it for a few days. I would get it back. They kept catching me," he admitted. "I think in the eighth grade they took my phone for a year." 
 Eventually, like any teenager, there came a point in Porter's childhood where he had had enough and decided to rebel. He recalled running away for hours at a time because he was mad, before eventually returning.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Related: "Dropping N-bombs and F-bombs" – Former NBA champion explains why Anthony Edwards can't be the NBA's face 
 Lesson learned 
 Despite how strict Porter's parents were, the values they instilled eventually became something the Brooklyn Nets star has leaned on today when it comes to the dangers and temptations of social media as a professional athlete.
 He himself revealed that he has limited his screen time by giving his phone to his mother to avoid the temptation to talk to girls on Instagram. Not only that, but his Christian beliefs have also influenced his views on commitment and family, topics he has been outspoken about in recent years.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Ultimately, despite Porter's annoyance with how strict his parents were. There was a lesson to be learned, one that he continues to value today. It also explains the outspoken personality that is never afraid to voice his opinions on faith, relationships and everything else.
